title: Console onboarding: backend checklist state APIs + per-project persistence
author: Jada Williams
description:
Summary: Implements server-side persistence + CRUD APIs for Guided Onboarding checklist state (Phase 1: Hosted API). This is the backend counterpart to the Console checklist shell (PR #48211) and follows ADR-0137. We store checklist progress per org + project with step-level state and timestamps, and expose a narrow API surface to let the Console read/update state while keeping validation / admin override paths consistent.

Motivation: We need durable checklist progress across sessions/devices and support workflows (reset state), plus a place for backend validators (first successful request / streaming session) to mark steps complete. Client-only state proved too fragile for cohort rollouts and multi-project orgs.

What’s included:
- DB model + migration for onboarding checklist state (scoped to project_id, with org_id for auth + indexing)
- REST APIs (internal Console API gateway) for create/read/update:
  - POST /console/v1/projects/{project_id}/onboarding/checklist_state
  - GET  /console/v1/projects/{project_id}/onboarding/checklist_state
  - PATCH /console/v1/projects/{project_id}/onboarding/checklist_state
- Concurrency + idempotency semantics:
  - POST is idempotent (returns existing row for project if already created)
  - PATCH supports partial updates with optimistic concurrency via updated_at (If-Match-style) to prevent clobbering from multiple tabs
- Step schema:
  - step_id (string; e.g., api_key_created, first_successful_request)
  - status (not_started | in_progress | completed | skipped)
  - completed_at (server timestamp) and metadata (allowlisted; no PII)
- Security/RBAC:
  - Project-scoped authorization enforced at handler layer (requires console:project:write for POST/PATCH, console:project:read for GET)
  - Explicitly disallows cross-project reads even within same org
- Test coverage:
  - Handler unit tests (auth, not-found, idempotent create)
  - Model tests (unique constraints, indexes)
  - API contract tests for PATCH merge behavior

Non-goals (follow-ups):
- Telemetry emission/event schema is in ENG-23112 / PR #48255
- Admin override/reset endpoint is tracked separately (later PR) but this PR lays the model groundwork (INT-3309)
- Dedicated/Private onboarding state is out of scope

Implementation details:
- Storage: onboarding_checklist_states table with unique(project_id) and index(org_id, updated_at)
- Read model: API returns a normalized list of steps (stable ordering in server response to simplify client rendering)
- Update model: PATCH accepts { steps: [{ step_id, status, completed_at? }] } and merges per step_id; server sets completed_at when transitioning into completed without an explicit timestamp from the client
- Data minimization: step metadata is restricted to an allowlist (e.g., source=console|backend_validator, validator_version, last_error_code). No prompt content, no raw request/response bodies.

Changed areas (high-level):
- services/console-api/src/routes/onboarding_checklist_state.ts
- services/console-api/src/controllers/onboarding_checklist_state_controller.ts
- services/console-api/src/policies/rbac.ts (wiring for new permissions)
- services/console-api/src/models/onboarding_checklist_state.ts
- services/console-api/db/migrations/20260203_add_onboarding_checklist_states.sql
- services/console-api/src/openapi/console-api.yaml (adds endpoints + schemas)
- services/console-api/test/*

Example response (GET):
{
  "project_id": "proj_123",
  "version": "v1",
  "steps": [
    {"step_id": "api_key_created", "status": "completed", "completed_at": "2026-02-06T18:22:10Z"},
    {"step_id": "first_successful_request", "status": "in_progress", "completed_at": null}
  ],
  "updated_at": "2026-02-06T18:30:01Z"
}

Notes:
- This PR assumes the checklist step IDs are managed server-side as a controlled vocabulary for v1. We can extend to versioned step sets once we add GA iterations.
- We will likely add a small TTL/cleanup job later for abandoned projects; intentionally not included here to avoid policy decisions without PM signoff.

Testing:
- console-api unit tests
- migration applied against local dev DB
- manual curl tests in dev env (create/get/patch) with RBAC on/off

Rollout:
- Backwards compatible; endpoints are unused until the feature-flagged UI calls them. Safe to merge ahead of UI rollout.

Related:
- Linear: ENG-23111, ENG-23110
- ADR-0137 (state & validation approach)
- Support: INT-3309 (reset request; future admin endpoint)

Checklist:
- [x] OpenAPI updated + reviewed
- [x] Migration tested
- [x] RBAC enforced + negative tests
- [x] No customer prompt content stored
commits: console-api: implement create/get/patch handlers with RBAC
openapi: document checklist state endpoints + schemas
review_conversation:
Chloe Martin (requested changes): Can we guarantee POST is idempotent? We’re going to have multiple Console entry points that may race on first load. Also please ensure completed_at is always server-generated when status flips to completed.

Jada Williams (author): Updated POST to upsert on project_id and return existing row. For PATCH, server now sets completed_at when transitioning into completed and client doesn’t supply it. Added unit tests covering both cases.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (requested changes): RBAC: please confirm we’re checking membership/role at the project scope, not org-only. Also, ensure error responses don’t leak existence of other projects.

Jada Williams (author): RBAC now uses requireProjectPermission(project_id, ...) with no org-level fallback. For non-member access we return 404 to avoid resource enumeration. Added negative tests.

Nadia Rahman (comment): For step metadata, we should treat this as privacy-sensitive. Can we enforce an allowlist at the model boundary rather than trusting handlers?

Jada Williams (author): Added allowlist enforcement in the model serializer + shared validator. Handlers now reject unknown metadata keys with 400.

Dylan Brooks (approval): Looks good. Small nit: can we keep step ordering stable for UI? Otherwise we’ll re-sort client side.

Jada Williams (author): Implemented server-side ordering via configured step list for v1.

Approvals: Chloe Martin (approved), Kaitlyn Nguyen (approved), Dylan Brooks (approved), Nadia Rahman (approved).
release_notes: Internal: Added Console API endpoints + persistence for guided onboarding checklist state (per project).
